newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan firm to lift capital to $11.5 m on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan firm to lift capital to $11.5 m on bourse.

text.p: Morocco's leasing firm Maroc-Leasing is to increase its capital by 21 percent to 106 million dirhams ($11.5 million) through a floatation on the Casablanca stock market, a bourse official said on Thursday.
One lot of 212,660 shares will be sold to the public at a price of 230 dirhams per share from 17 to 21 February, 1997, the official said.
But 1.0 percent of the increased amount will be allocated to company employees, he added.
In an advertisement, Maroc-Leasing said a tranche of 106,330 shares or 10 percent of the capital, would be reserved for local and foreign investors including institutions.
The second tranche of 106,330 shares would be allocated to mutual funds.
The minimum subscription was set at five shares for the public and private investors and 1,000 shares for mutual funds, the firm said.
Established in Casablanca in 1965, Maroc-Leasing now has capital of 84 million shares.
Morocco's second largest conglomerate Societe Nationale d'Investissement and Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique hold respectively 35 and 65 percent of the firm's stock.
The firm showed a net profit of 8.68 million dirhams in the first nine months of 1996 against 18.1 million dirhams for the whole year of 1995.
Maroc-Leasing expects a net profit of 14.9 million dirhams in 1996, officials said.
It is the second private firm to be floated on the bourse, after credit firm Credor, since the market reform programme was launched by the government in 1993.

"The leasing business in Morocco represents an estimated 2.0 billion dirhams turnover annually...It grows at an average of 18.4 percent per year," Ali Marrakshi, the firm's managing director told a news conference on Thursday.
The firm hold up to 21 percent of the market stake, Marrakshi said.
The sale of Maroc-Leasing stake on the bourse aimed at "financing a part of the firm's investments in 1997," he added.
Maroc-Leasing is expected to be listed on the Casablanca stock exchange on February 27, 1997.
Established in 1929, the Casablanca bourse has 47 listed stocks, including eight banks,
